silo_relevance: This survey is highly relevant to portfolio_optimization because it devotes a dedicated section to quantum portfolio selection and rebalancing, including annealing, QRAM/HHL-style formulations, and VQE-based approaches. It also provides the classical optimization framing, evaluation metrics, and practical limitations that determine whether these methods can be useful for real portfolio construction.

key_points.point: The paper defines portfolio optimization in the standard mean-variance / constrained allocation sense and highlights the Sharpe ratio as a key evaluation metric.
key_points.silo_note: This is the core problem formulation for portfolio_optimization, so it anchors how the reviewed quantum methods are meant to be judged.

key_points.point: The survey’s portfolio section focuses on quantum annealing and related optimization methods, including QAOA-style combinatorial optimization and quantum portfolio formulations using QRAM/HHL.
key_points.silo_note: These are directly relevant because they target asset selection and allocation as an optimization problem rather than a prediction task.

key_points.point: Reported portfolio results include optimized reverse annealing being more than 100x faster than forward annealing, gate-model rebalancing being feasible on NISQ hardware, and solutions within 5% of optimal adjusted returns on a small portfolio.
key_points.silo_note: These are the most concrete performance claims for portfolio_optimization, showing both potential speed and solution quality.

key_points.point: The survey repeatedly benchmarks quantum portfolio methods against classical solvers and notes that VQE can come close to exact solutions under suitable hyperparameters.
key_points.silo_note: For portfolio_optimization, the key question is whether quantum methods can match or improve classical optimizers on comparable instances.

key_points.point: The paper also stresses major constraints for portfolio applications, especially NISQ noise, limited qubits, and hardware instability, and notes that some portfolio demonstrations were only successful on very small problems.
key_points.silo_note: This tempers the practical relevance of the reported portfolio gains and indicates that current methods are still far from large-scale portfolio deployment.
